claims.text: Superconducting properties in uncharacterized high-entropy alloys are governed by a balance between electron-phonon coupling and disorder-induced scattering.
Increasing the content of titanium-rich heavy transition metals lowers phonon frequencies and increases the electron-phonon coupling constant.
Composition changes that preserve a homogeneous single phase can modulate the superconducting transition temperature.
Substitution beyond an optimal disorder threshold causes pair-breaking scattering that reduces Tc.
The proposed starting material is a single-phase, Nb-Ta-dominated high-entropy alloy containing at least five elements at concentrations of at least 5 at.% each.
Substituting Nb and Ta with Ti, Zr, or Hf while retaining a single-phase solid solution provides a controlled compositional intervention.
Identical high-temperature annealing guarantees complete mixing and homogeneity.
Atomic-size differences introduced by substitution produce local lattice distortions and variations in interatomic distances.
The substitution-induced lattice distortions alter the phonon density of states.
Changes in the phonon density of states affect electron-phonon coupling strength.
Replacing Nb-Ta with Ti, Zr, or Hf modifies the electronic density of states at the Fermi level and the phonon spectrum.
Heavier substituent elements soften phonon modes and thereby enhance the electron-phonon coupling responsible for superconducting pairing.
Greater atomic-size variation and chemical disorder enhance electron scattering.
Superconductivity is optimized when the benefit from increased electron-phonon coupling exceeds the detrimental effect of scattering.
Moderate substitution should shift Tc and may increase it up to an optimum.
Moderate substitution should also change the superconducting gap and critical current density relative to the baseline.
Excessive substitution should increase disorder and reduce Tc.
The proposed mechanism applies only when the alloy remains a single-phase solid solution without phase separation or ordering.
Replacing approximately 30-40 at.% of the Nb-Ta content is a moderate range that can preserve the solid-solution state and avoid excessive disorder.
A lack of systematic and reproducible changes in Tc, superconducting gap, and critical current density would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that Tc is measured at temperatures well below the nominal Tc, whereas determining Tc by resistivity or susceptibility requires a temperature sweep through the superconducting transition.
